title: CelluWeave A: Wet compression of cellulose–alginate sheets
researchQuestion: Evaluation of the properties of nonliving cellulose–alginate hydrogel sheets under different calcium chloride concentrations.
mainFindings: The 50 mmol/L condition resulted in a mean compressive modulus of 42.0 kPa, shape retention of 96%, and water uptake of 10.0 g water per g dry sheet.
The 75 mmol/L condition resulted in a mean compressive modulus of 56.0 kPa and shape retention of 88%.
Higher compressive modulus was associated with poorer shape retention.
The 50 mmol/L condition had a mean compressive modulus of 42.0 kPa and 96% shape retention.
The 75 mmol/L condition had a mean compressive modulus of 56.0 kPa and 88% shape retention.
methods: calcium chloride bath 50 mmol/L for 10 minutes
Compression was measured wet, after 24 hours of equilibration, at 10% strain
methodsSummary: Hydrogel sheets composed of 2.0% w/v alginate and 0.8% w/v cellulose were crosslinked in calcium chloride baths (50 or 75 mmol/L) for 10 minutes, equilibrated for 24 hours, and then tested for compression at 10% strain.
